Use dimension annotations and corresponding views to assess the decorative bounding boxes. D1 and D2 must each remain within 35 × 35 × 4 mm, and every depicted pair arrangement within 70 × 45 × 4 mm. Carrier depth is excluded. Smaller dimensions and different compliant arrangements are allowed; an oversized module, excessive decorative layering or an oversized displayed pair fails.

The drawings collectively identify where each chosen material, colour and finish is used and show softened exposed edges and contact points. Decorative stock is limited to uncoated brushed natural-colour 316L steel, M1 at 1.0 mm, and/or solid through-coloured acrylic, M2 at 2.0 mm with a matte or polished finish. The link uses integral tabs, slots or formed features in these materials. Either material alone, both together and layering within the depth limit are allowed. Unallocated materials, sharp exposed contact geometry or an added purchased linking component fail.

Read the carrier annotations and geometry as fixed supplied parts: P has a 24 × 6 × 2 mm plate, a 7 mm closed rear projection and a 1.5–3.0 mm fabric range; C has a 28 × 8 × 2 mm plate, a 9 mm projection and a 0.6–1.2 mm fabric range. Both retain two M2 threaded holes at local centres (−6, 0) and (+6, 0). Require the correct plate dimensions and mounting geometry; any stated fabric ranges must agree. Screw length and thread engagement may remain open. Redesigning the supplied attachment faces or substituting incompatible carriers fails.

Require identifiable front, rear and side views of both D1 and D2, one assembled pair, readable actual dimensions and explicit material, sheet-thickness, colour and finish allocations. Both required phrases must appear on this drawing. Dimensions must describe the chosen design rather than merely restating maximum envelopes. Either permitted material or their combination is acceptable; missing views, missing specifications or contradictory dimensions fail.

Verify two dimensioned 2.4 mm clearance holes on each module, separated by 12 mm, with room behind each for the larger C plate. The carrier projections must be measured from the mounting face. Views must reveal usable screwdriver access off clothing, the protected needle catch, clip opening space and soft garment-contact pads. Detail or exploded views are acceptable; obscured mechanisms, blocked access or decorative interference fail.

Show D1 and D2 each mounting to either carrier using the two supplied screws, including the screw removal and replacement needed for exchange. A paired rear view must identify the carrier-mounted module and the second module supported by the link. Both link attachment and release must be understandable as hand operations. One carrier per pair and unobstructed mounting holes are required; two-carrier support, a tool-dependent link or an unexplained release fails.

Read each board and inset against these records: W01, D1+D2, wearer's left wool-jacket lapel, P, 2.4 mm; W02, D1 alone, scarf edge, C, 0.8 mm; W03, D2 alone, wearer's right wool-jacket lapel, P, 2.4 mm; W04, D1+D2, shirt placket, C, 1.0 mm. Require all four record labels and a reverse/contact inset identifying the correct carrier on every board. Adult wearing depictions must retain the garments and placement landmarks from wearer-wardrobe.png and match the drawings' module shapes, proportions, material allocations and attachment locations. Lighting, clothing colour, framing and adult model identity may vary. A wrong record, missing inset, altered garment identity or inconsistent jewellery scale fails.
